title: Active-passive recovery runbook for Token Store with automated restore harness and canary validation
creator: Connor Liu
description: Purpose: Create a focused active-passive DR runbook for the Token Store service (auth.tokens) that codifies backup/restore validation, automated restore harnesses for nightly verification, and a short-form canary validation sequence for scheduled failover drills. Scope intentionally limited to Token Store because it is both latency-sensitive and has strict integrity requirements; the design will be reusable for other small stateful services.
background: Token Store holds short-lived auth tokens and refresh state for hosted API customers. Current passive DR exists but lacks reproducible restore validation and a safe canary validation sequence. We need deterministic, low-risk drills that prove RPO/RTO targets (RPO <= 5m, RTO <= 5m for critical ops) while minimizing customer impact via traffic steering, circuit breakers, and load-shedding policies.
goals: Document an operator-run and an automated path for full DB snapshot restore into the passive region
Implement nightly restore-harness that validates backup integrity and end-to-end behavior against a synthetic tenant
Define circuit-breaker and load-shedding thresholds for the Token Store during failover to prevent cascading overload
Create a short canary test suite (smoke + correctness) that runs after traffic is switched to passive
Provide clear rollback and re-sync steps to return to active region after drill
acceptance_criteria: Nightly restore-harness runs for 14 days with zero corruption detected on synthetic tenant
Runbook steps are executable by two SREs and take < 30 minutes to complete from start to canary green
Circuit-breaker metrics (5xx rate, latency P95) remain within defined thresholds during scheduled failover
Post-drill checklist and automated snapshot tags are produced and linked to the incident record
runbook_steps: Pre-check: Verify latest DB snapshot exists in s3://redwood-backups/tokenstore/YYYYMMDD-HHMM and checksum matches manifest
Pre-check: Confirm passive region cluster is at runtime-1.21 and has compatible kernel flags (kv-cache enabled, quantized kernels installed)
Pre-check: Increase observability retention for tokenstore.* traces by 48h for drill window
Step 0 (communication): Announce drill in #oncall and send email to impacted customers at least 48h prior for non-experimental tenants
Step 1 (quiesce writes): Apply write-blocking flag to active tokenstore (api call: POST /admin/freeze?service=tokenstore) and wait for inflight ops to drain (monitor inflight_requests < 5)
Step 2 (snapshot export): Trigger snapshot export job (k8s job: tokenstore-export-v2) and verify s3 copy completed and checksums OK

Step 3 (restore into passive): Run restore-harness script (scripts/restore_harness.sh --target-region=eu-west-1 --snapshot=s3://...); harness performs DB restore into a dedicated restore namespace tokenstore-restore-<ts>
Step 4 (data validation): Harness runs validation suite: checksum compare, sample token redemption test, index/seq integrity checks. Failures escalate to runbook lead
Step 5 (canary switch): Add passive region to routing with small percentage (5%) using smart-routing API and enable canary traffic; monitor for 2 minutes
Step 6 (canary tests): Run canary suite 1 (liveness), suite 2 (token create/refresh), suite 3 (revocation) against canary traffic; require zero data-loss and <250ms median latency
Step 7 (gradual cutover): If canary green, gradually increase traffic to 100% over 10 minutes while maintaining circuit-breaker thresholds; if anomalies detected, immediate rollback to active
Step 8 (post-cutover validations): Run full smoke tests, reconcile counters (issued vs redeemed tokens), and ensure metrics dashboards show no unexplained gaps
Step 9 (cleanup): Decommission tokenstore-restore namespace after snapshot of restored state to s3://redwood-backups/post-dr-tokenstore/<ts> and label backup as 'dr-tested'
Step 10 (postmortem): Create incident note, attach harness logs, snapshot manifests, and a short summary within 24h
circuit_breaker_and_load_shedding: During any partial or full failover we will rely on two layered protections: 1) service-level circuit breakers that trip at 10% 5xx rate over a 1m window or P95 latency > 1200ms; 2) platform ingress rate limiter that steps down allowed RPS per-customer by 30% when circuit-breaker engaged. For the Token Store we add a conservative token-issue rate cap per-tenant (default 200 RPS) that can be lowered dynamically via feature flag. All CB events are to be logged to #cb-alerts and emit an internal metric tokenstore.cb.trips. The runbook includes safe exact commands to lower caps via the config service (POST /config/tokenstore/limits).
restore_validation_harness: The harness is a set of CI jobs and a k8s Job that performs: 1) restore DB snapshot into an isolated namespace; 2) run data integrity checks (checksums, unique index validation); 3) run blackbox functional tests against a synthetic tenant seeded at snapshot time; 4) run TTL/expiry and background-job validation; 5) tear down the namespace on success. Harness artifacts (stdout, logs, validation report) are uploaded to GCS and linked automatically to the nightly job in BigQuery records.
canary_test_suite: Auth flow: create token -> redeem token -> refresh token sequence with assertions on token payload
Revocation: issue + revoke + ensure redemption fails
Expiration: create short-lived token and assert expiry works after TTL window
Rate-limits: try to exceed per-tenant cap to ensure load-shedding path returns 429 and not 5xx
metrics_and_alerting: Dashboards to verify: tokenstore.latency.P50/P95, tokenstore.5xx.rate, tokenstore.inflight_requests, tokenstore.cb.trips, tokenstore.restore.duration. Create a temporary composite alert during the drill that fires if 5xx rate > 5% for 5m or P95 > 800ms. On alert, runbook instructs immediate rollback and contact on-call via phone tree.
rollback_plan: If any canary test fails or the composite alert fires: 1) revert traffic-weighting using smart-routing API to point 100% at active region; 2) re-enable writes on active tokenstore (unfreeze); 3) mark passive restore namespace as 'failed-<ts>' and collect debug artifacts (db-dump sample, pprof heap/CPU), 4) escalate to platform reliability with priority P0 and open an incident in the incident tracker. Include a mandatory post-drill pause of 24h to analyze root cause before reattempting.
operational_playbooks_and_commands: Freeze writes: curl -X POST https://admin.internal/tokenstore/freeze -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN'
Trigger export: kubectl -n tokenstore run tokenstore-export --image=redwood/tokenstore-export:2.3 -- /export --out s3://...
Lower tenant caps: curl -X POST https://config.internal/tokenstore/limits -d '{"tenant":"*","rps":100 }'
test_plan_and_schedule: Nightly: automated restore-harness against synthetic tenant at 02:00 UTC (non-business hours) -> success report to #dr-tests
Quarterly: full scheduled failover drill with real traffic windowed to low-traffic day (runbook owners oncall) -> followed by 2-day analysis
Pre-release: any platform release that touches storage or snapshot code must run harness in staging before promoting to production
roles_and_contacts: Backup owner: SRE - backup team (oncall rotation: backup-rotation)
progress_updates: 2025-09-12: Draft created by Connor Liu outlining scope and initial goals.
2025-09-18: Backup owner confirmed snapshot naming scheme and S3 lifecycle won't interfere with test snapshots; added 'dr-tested' tagging convention.
2025-09-25: Initial harness prototype merged (PR #4823). Harness currently restores to tokenstore-restore-* and runs checksum validators. Needs canary suite integration.
2025-09-30: CB thresholds proposed by reliability team; added load-shedding commands. PM review requested for customer communication plan.
2025-10-03: Security requested review for synthetic tenant data seeding; marked security_review_required=true and added staging-only KMS key usage. Assigned to Marta for next steps.
notes_for_reviewers: Please review the canary test time windows and CB thresholds. Security needs to approve synthetic tenant seeding and KMS usage for harness. Ops: validate that the smart-routing API accepts the gradual weight increase payload described. If any team has objections to the 5m RTO target, annotate with constraints and suggested changes.
postmortem_requirements: Every scheduled drill must produce a short postmortem within 72h containing: what changed, timelines, observed metrics vs expected SLOs, root cause analysis for anomalies, and action items with owners and due dates. Attach harness logs and snapshot manifests.
